title: Dragon's Lair
build: Software Projects disk, alternate D64 with LA–LJ files

records.c: The first copied byte in the scene record is $05. The caller starts executing one byte later.
Save and reload the caller stack pointer, set the room palette, install the raster handler and enable sprites 5–7 in the bank at $4000. Apply the colour lookup and initialize the tentacle state.
Restore the stack and use the three room palette colours at $D021–$D023. Fill the glyph and score pointers, install the room raster behaviour and enable sprites 5–7.
Call the delay and update routine at $2914 with A equal to three before selecting the next overlay.
Select successive overlay records and sprite 0 shapes. Apply 30 leftward and 12 upward steps between the timed pose selections, then continue to the next movement test.
Reset the palette for sprites 1–3 and apply three more overlay and shape pairs with movement between them. After the timed approach, select movement mode and preset 4 for the next creature pass.

Reset the input retry delay and begin the repeated wait and creature update. Once the movement phase is clear and its counter is below ten, test for fire using the input matcher. A matching press enters the next sequence.
Set mode 1, initialize a creature pass with preset 5 and apply overlay 14. Move the pose left and up, then use the direction and timing routines before selecting the next creature mode.
Set the new mode and creature preset, update its position between delay calls and test the fire input in the active timing window.
Request sound $87, select overlay 14 and run timed move steps. Disable sprites after the last overlay animation and return through the saved scene stack after decrementing $25.

Decrement the frame delay. On reload, use the toggle at $2A5C to step the sprite 4 frame pointer in opposite directions unless the movement mode is two. Select the backwards pixel copy when $2A58 is nonzero.
Copy three bytes per row through the source and destination pointers and decrement each pointer by three. The row counter controls the extra step between 21-row sprite records.
Initialize the source at $6C83 and destination at $6C80, then shift successive three-byte sprite rows toward the start of the buffer. The value at $2A5E selects the initial counter at $2DAD.
Copy three bytes per row and advance both pointers. After 21 rows advance again to skip the sprite record padding.
Save the requested mirror orientation at $03EF and call the resident mirror helper for nine consecutive frames beginning two slots after the pointer selected at $29D5.
Request sound $8A, multiply the selection by 20 and use a table from $29D8 to set sprite coordinates. The $2A5E mode changes which subset is written.

Move the staged sprite coordinates and raster positions upward in 55 iterations. The loop clears three consecutive bytes at a time in the sprite buffer beginning at $6C80 and waits through the CIA2 delay between iterations.
Read the two VIC coordinate bytes for sprite 2 and write them to sprite 1.
Wait through the scene timing routine with count $32, call the shared routine at $0ECD and jump back to scene initialization.
Wait for the count passed in A, show the resident failure interstitial and jump to the room restart at $1E04.
Count down A in $2DAF. Complement $2A5B on each iteration and wait and poll the joystick on the zero phase.
Count down A in $2DAF and call $256D after each timer wait and joystick sample on alternate phases of $2A5B.
Wait and sample the joystick A times, invoking $2942 after each timer delay.
Every third call, AND bytes at $6C81–$6D3F with a changing mask made by XORing CIA1 timer A low and the raster counter.
Read CIA1 port A with all keyboard column outputs high, invert the active-low bits and compare with the previous sample at $2A60 before updating that byte.
Use A as the exact expected joystick mask. Invert the active-low sample, honour the retry delay, and give a mismatching nonzero input a delay of $14 and sound $89.
Set the colours of sprites 1, 2 and 3 to 1.
Three bytes copied from the start of the Weapons Room cell animation state at $316C–$316E.
First seven little-endian Weapons Room screen cell addresses from $316F–$317C. The original animation indexes them with its phase counter.
Two zero bytes occupy the position of the eighth address in the Weapons Room cell address table.
Five cell animation character codes from the Weapons Room array at $317F–$3183. The Tentacle Room band index immediately follows.
Cleared by the first raster handler at $2B36. The later raster handlers increment it while advancing through the sprite overlays.
The setup at $1E65 and $1E68 clears these two adjacent bytes before selecting the room colour lookup.
The action matcher counts down from $14 after receiving an unexpected direction.
The creature setup stores its selection here before multiplying it by 20.
Two zero slots after the setup record index. The motion-mode lookup uses the following three bytes at $29D5 as VIC frame pointers.
Three frame values indexed by the creature motion mode. The frame selects both a pointer and a pixel buffer address.
Position record 0 for the creature and nearby sprites. The first eight bytes at $29D8 supply sprite coordinates selected by $27DB. Later fields supply position presets for the scripted poses.
Position record 1 for the creature and nearby sprites. The first eight bytes at $29EC supply sprite coordinates selected by $27DB. Later fields supply position presets for the scripted poses.
Position record 2 for the creature and nearby sprites. The first eight bytes at $2A00 supply sprite coordinates selected by $27DB. Later fields supply position presets for the scripted poses.
Position record 3 for the creature and nearby sprites. The first eight bytes at $2A14 supply sprite coordinates selected by $27DB. Later fields supply position presets for the scripted poses.
Position record 4 for the creature and nearby sprites. The first eight bytes at $2A28 supply sprite coordinates selected by $27DB. Later fields supply position presets for the scripted poses.
Position record 5 for the creature and nearby sprites. The first eight bytes at $2A3C supply sprite coordinates selected by $27DB. Later fields supply position presets for the scripted poses.
Frame value saved from the mode table by $27EB.
Four authored zero slots between the base VIC sprite pointer and the two-byte pixel buffer address. The setup writes that address at $2A55–$2A56.
Pixel buffer pointer computed from the selected sprite frame at $27FA. Its high byte is advanced by $40 for the active VIC bank.
One zero slot immediately after the pixel buffer address and before the two live shift-state bytes at $2A58–$2A59.
The sprite advance tests this value to choose the backwards copy or the alternate update.
The activity and phase byte read by the creature update loops and coordinate calculations.
The movement counter compared with ten by the input windows and used as a coordinate offset.
The timed wait paths read this byte to compare against the active raster phase.
The sprite updater flips this byte to alternate between adjacent sprite 4 frame pointers.
Decremented by $256D and reloaded with four before alternating the creature pose.
Selects a sprite-frame entry and controls whether the position setter updates six or eight VIC coordinate registers.
The pixel updater at $2942 decrements this countdown and reloads it to three before processing the sprite buffer.
Multiply the pose index A by 90, add $3200 and copy the resulting record to $44–$9D after synchronizing to raster.
Multiply A by 18 and use the result to select the positions, colours, pointers and expansion masks for sprites 4–7.
Use A to select sprite 0 coordinates, expansion bits and a packed source. Select pointer $A9 and build its 64-byte image at $6A40 from a zero count and trailing literals.
Apply pose group 1 to the registers and pointers for sprites 5–7. Install $2B85 for the next split, with the line selected by zero-page byte $99.
Apply pose group 2 to the registers and pointers for sprites 5–7. Install $2BC5 for the next split, with the line selected by zero-page byte $9A.
Apply pose group 3 to the registers and pointers for sprites 5–7. Install $2C05 for the next split, with the line selected by zero-page byte $9B.
Apply pose group 4 to the registers and pointers for sprites 5–7. Install $2C45 for the next split, with the line selected by zero-page byte $9C.
Apply pose group 5 to the registers and pointers for sprites 5–7. Install $2C85 for the next split, with the line selected by zero-page byte $9D.
Apply pose group 6 to the registers and pointers for sprites 5–7. Install $2B34 for the next split, with the line selected by constant 1.
Wait for the shared raster synchronization and install $2B34 in the IRQ target at $42/$43.
Set the source to $7400 and the destination to $4000 before entering the shared character matrix copy.
Use source $4000 and destination $0400. The common copy preserves the primary sprite pointer slots and then reapplies the scene colour lookup.
Increase the low X coordinates of the three sprites in each of the six pose groups and of sprite 0. Merge its high-X bit after wrap.
Use A as the repetition count. Decrease the three low-X coordinates in each of the six saved pose bands and decrease X for sprite 0.
Decrement the low X registers for sprites 4–7 and sprite 0 once per count in A.
Increment the low X registers for sprites 4–7 and sprite 0 once per count in A.
Decrement the Y registers for sprites 4–7 and sprite 0 once per count in A.
Increase both sprite 0 Y and the four coordinate registers for sprites 4–7, using A as the repetition count.
The sprite shift state begins with $00, $00 and $07 after the coordinate-update routine. The row adjustment counters used by the pixel loops start at the next byte, $2DAB.
The forward and reverse copies use this counter to apply a one-byte adjustment to the sprite source pointer after a group of rows.
Counter for the separate one-byte adjustment of the destination pointer in the forward and reverse sprite row copies.
Counts remaining source adjustments during the sprite row shift. The movement mode selects the initialization value.
The erase loop at $2886 starts this byte at 55. The shared alternating wait at $28FB also uses it as a countdown.
Nineteen little-endian source pointers indexed by twice the shape selector in the sprite 0 builder at $2AD5.
Nineteen low-X and Y pairs selected for sprite 0 by the shape selector.
One sprite 0 horizontal expansion bit per shape selector, merged into $D01D.
One sprite 0 vertical expansion bit per shape selector, merged into $D017.
Packed sprite 0 frame. The initial count 35 selects the leading zero bytes. The following 29 bytes through $2E44 are literals for the frame at $6A40.
Packed sprite 0 frame. The initial count 39 selects the leading zero bytes. The following 25 bytes through $2E5D are literals for the frame at $6A40.
Packed sprite 0 frame. The initial count 35 selects the leading zero bytes. The following 29 bytes through $2E7A are literals for the frame at $6A40.
Packed sprite 0 frame. The initial count 60 selects the leading zero bytes. The following 4 bytes through $2E7E are literals for the frame at $6A40.
Packed sprite 0 frame. The initial count 23 selects the leading zero bytes. The following 41 bytes through $2EA7 are literals for the frame at $6A40.
Packed sprite 0 frame. The initial count 45 selects the leading zero bytes. The following 19 bytes through $2EBA are literals for the frame at $6A40.
Packed sprite 0 frame. The initial count 37 selects the leading zero bytes. The following 27 bytes through $2ED5 are literals for the frame at $6A40.
Packed sprite 0 frame. The initial count 57 selects the leading zero bytes. The following 7 bytes through $2EDC are literals for the frame at $6A40.
Packed sprite 0 frame. The initial count 15 selects the leading zero bytes. The following 49 bytes through $2F0D are literals for the frame at $6A40.
Packed sprite 0 frame. The initial count 24 selects the leading zero bytes. The following 40 bytes through $2F35 are literals for the frame at $6A40.
Sixteen 18-byte records selected by $2A83. Each gives positions, colours and frame pointers for sprites 4–7 and the two expansion masks.
This scene record ends with the eleven byte marker copied by the unpacker at $0DDE.
The first page of the screen matrix for the background in VIC bank $4000. Its character codes index the scene colour lookup when the display is initialized.
Screen matrix offsets $100–$1FF. The VIC reads these as character codes and the palette routine processes a page at a time.
Screen matrix offsets $200–$2FF. The screen maps into the glyph data at $7800.
The last page of the screen matrix, including the hardware sprite pointers at $43F8–$43FF.
First sixteen sprite records after the room screen. The rendered pieces include curved and extended movement shapes.
Sixteen shapes including bent limbs and head silhouettes, laid out in 64-byte records.
A run of sprite fragments of legs and arms for the tentacle-room player animation.
Sixteen shapes continuing the pose table, including several paired lower body figures.
Middle bank of rendered movement fragments, with a long curved arm at pointer $59.
Sixteen 64-byte VIC sprite records in bank $4000 for pointers $60–$6F. Each has 63 pixel bytes and a trailing zero in the scene image.
Tentacle-room sprite part masks for pointers $70–$7F. The leg shapes change orientation between successive records.
Sixteen records including the alternately curled and outstretched body pieces at the end of this range.
Middle-to-high range of body-part masks, with some blank records between the visible pieces.
Sprite parts around pointer $A9, which the scene writes to $43F8 at $2AE6.

Two 64-byte VIC sprite shape slots in bank $4000. Pointer $B0 selects the first shape and pointer $B1 selects the second. These records follow the $A0–$AF shape group and precede the writable buffer at $6C80.
The scene filters bytes $6C81–$6D3F at $295F, using the timer and raster as a mask during the sprite-erasure effect.
The unpacked picture stream initializes $6D40–$6EFF to zero. These bytes are still zero in the play capture.
Sixteen extended and folded shapes near the end of the room sprite bank, spaced by $40 bytes.
High sprite slots including claw-like, curved and extended tentacle shapes.
Colour table whose entries are indexed by the bytes in the room screen matrix. The scene selects its page at $1E6D.
The scene character glyph store for VIC bank $4000 and character-base bits 3–1 of $D018 set to 7. A character occupies eight consecutive bytes.
The top half of this scene set, from character code $80. The eight-byte glyph slots are used for the scene-specific objects and screen details.
The LE bytes at $B7B4–$B7B4 follow the last source token required by the scene picture decoder and precede the repeated disk fill.
Repeated $06 bytes at $B7B5–$B80F, after the input consumed by the scene picture decode.
